liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Eyes of the World** (3 reviews): Reviewer calls Eyes the highlight of the pre-drums portion of the second set; Reviewer counts it among the best Eyes they have heard, gorgeous [20][25][27]
- **Candyman** (2 reviews): The line about telling everybody you meet is sung especially well; Special version with unusual keyboard textures: sax-like sounds, choir sounds and warm pads, unlike the usual piano [19][27]
- **Attics of My Life** (2 reviews): The encore is nice but under-sung; the band had last played it a year and a half earlier; Hearing Attics close the show made the listener feel it was something bigger than life [20][22]
- **Touch of Grey** (1 review): Bob enters a verse early, which seems to amuse Jerry and spur a spirited finish [19]
- **Saint of Circumstance** (1 review): Called about the only weak spot of the second set [23]
- **Dark Star Jam** (1 review): Reviewer points to the Dark Star jam in the run's first show as a standout [22]
- **Space** (1 review): Reviewer especially enjoys Space, along with the Dark Star Jam and Drums [27]
- **The Other One** (1 review): Haunting, especially the progression of notes leading into Wharf Rat [23]

## Setlist highlights

- **Attics of My Life**: back after 116 archived shows (527 days) [31]

## The recordings

- **gd91-09-08.sbd.ashley.1069.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 20 songs; 170 min; rated 4.2/5 by 15 [1]. Said about its sound: Great sound, with every instrument coming through loud and clear [23]
- **gd1991-09-08.aud.andrewf.88002.sbeok.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 21 songs; 171 min [4]
- **gd1991-09-08.149846.sbd.cm.miller.flac16**: soundboard; 19 songs; 170 min [5]
- **gd1991-09-08.sbd.hinko.75772.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 19 songs; 169 min [7]

## Around the show

- Listener attended and jotted a note on their handwritten setlist praising Lesh's playing; sees the MSG run as great [21]
- Hornsby's presence acted as a catalyst for the band in the period after Brent [22]
- As Touch of Grey began, someone behind the listener broke glow sticks and threw them over the crowd [26]
- Considered an underrated show within the historic Madison Square Garden run [25]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd91-09-08.sbd.ashley.1069.sbeok.shnf**: source: DSBD> DAT> CD [1]. Also: Soundboard recording transferred from digital source to DAT to CD via Jay Ashley, with a flaw noted in comments [1]
- **gd1991-09-08.aud.andrewf.88002.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Andrew F; transferred by Andrew F; source: Schoeps CMC3/MK4 (ORTF) > unknown power supply > Panasonic SV-255 (lead deck) > Coax SPDIF > Casio DA-7 dat (first deck out) > Agfa Dat tape. Mics on 7-foot… [4]. Also: Audience source; fades made in Soundforge, TLH used for FLAC compression and checksums, seamless break between discs two and three [4]
- **gd1991-09-08.149846.sbd.cm.miller.flac16**: taped by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering By Charlie Miller  May 2, 2020; source: SBD > Cassette Master (TDK SA-X100) [5]. Also: Recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; several sets of masters were combined to complete the show [5]
- **gd1991-09-08.sbd.hinko.75772.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Darryl Hinko; source: DSBD > DAT > CDA [7]. Also: Transfer trims some repeated material between Drums and Space; first set fits on one disc [7]
